extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers preparing ERC Starting Grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining whether an applicant meets ERC Starting Grant eligibility (timing, degree type, career-break extensions, documentation) and practical rules to avoid administrative rejection. Focused on who is eligible, how to claim extensions, and procedural traps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility window (standard rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Starting Grant window is 2 to 7 years after the PhD defense date (not graduation/award date). For the 2025 call, defended between 1 Jan 2018 and 31 Dec 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate from the certified date of successful PhD defense. If your viva/defense was in Oct 2019 but the diploma was issued later, use Oct 2019. Using the award/graduation date is a frequent and costly mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD defense date as reference (2023 rule change)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERC uses the certified date of successful PhD defense as the single, verifiable reference point for eligibility rather than the PhD award/graduation date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no formal defense/viva exists in your system, obtain written confirmation from the awarding institution that no defense occurred and state when the PhD was officially approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: First PhD counts rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If you hold multiple doctorates, the earliest doctorate (first PhD) determines the Starting Grant eligibility window, regardless of field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a PhD in 2015 and a second doctorate in 2020 means eligibility counts from 2015. This rule applies 'regardless of field' and can affect career pivots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional doctorates are not PhD-equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: First-professional degrees (JD, MD, PharmD, etc.) will not be considered PhD-equivalent in themselves even if title 'Doctor' is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holders of professional doctorates must meet additional conditions (see MD-specific rules) or hold/claim a research PhD to use the PhD-based window.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD-specific eligibility (medical doctors)
rubrics_metrics.description: An MD alone does not qualify as a PhD; applicants need either (a) a separate research PhD, or (b) documented research experience plus an appointment requiring doctoral equivalency (e.g., professorship or postdoc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For MDs without a PhD, the eligibility window shifts to 4-9 years after the medical degree, calculated as MD completion date plus two years. If you hold both MD and PhD, calculate from whichever degree yields earlier eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career break extensions — general principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERC offers eligibility extensions for career breaks (parental leave, illness, clinical training, service, disasters, asylum, etc.). Extensions are additive and there is no overall maximum except where specifically capped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions can be combined (e.g., maternity + clinical training). Only clinical training has a specific cap (4 years). Claim all applicable extensions; the ERC encourages applicants to do so and panels will use them as contextual information rather than penalize applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maternity leave extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Flat-rate extension of 18 months per child, whether the child was born before or after the PhD defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you can document longer actual leave (maternity plus parental leave combined), the ERC grants the documented amount instead of the flat rate. Example: two children with 40 months documented leave => 40 months extension (not 36). Part-time parental work counts proportionally (e.g., 50% for 12 months = 6 months extension). Required documentation: birth certificates, passports, family books; for claims >18 months per child provide HR-signed employer documents certifying exact leave dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paternity leave extension
rubrics_metrics.description: No flat-rate; extensions equal the documented actual leave taken by the father.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires employer documentation specifying exact start and end dates. The ERC treats paternity leave asymmetrically due to international policy variation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illness extension (long-term illness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions for personal long-term illness or caring responsibilities apply only for incidents lasting over 90 days (continuous or aggregate for the same condition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires employer certification AND medical documentation from hospitals, doctors, or insurance companies explaining the long-term nature of the condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical training extension (capped)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical training after the PhD qualifies for an extension up to a maximum of 4 years (the only explicitly capped extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training must be structured and supervised (formal training program). Standard hospital doctor service without formal training program status does not qualify. Employer/hospital certification specifying training type and dates is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other qualifying extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Other documented interruptions that can produce extensions include national/military service, major disasters (geological events, floods, armed conflicts causing ≥90 days inability to work), seeking asylum, and (new in 2026) disability and gender-based violence (minimum 90 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For seeking asylum, the extension runs from the application date until the decision or issuance of a residence permit. COVID-19 lockdowns alone do not qualify, though COVID-related personal illness may qualify under illness rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions documentation procedure (how to claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: All extensions must be claimed in Part A (Section 5 - 'Other Questions') and supporting documentation uploaded as a single PDF labeled 'Annex 1 - Extension Request' including the official ERC template cover page stating the duration requested and explaining the calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Admissibility and Eligibility Review Committee (ERCEA) reviews extension requests after the deadline and may request additional information if documentation appears incomplete. Prepare clear, legible scans and employer/medical certificates as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation requirements by extension type (specific docs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different extension types have specific documentary evidence requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maternity: birth certificates, passports, family books; >18 months requires HR-signed employer documents. Paternity: employer documentation with start/end dates. Illness: employer certification + medical documentation. Clinical training: employer/hospital certification specifying training type and dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility and administrative traps
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative mistakes can cause admissibility rejection even when scientific merit is strong.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common errors: using award/graduation date instead of defense date; wrong template version; blurry/low-quality scans of support letters; inconsistent project title/acronym across documents; failure to upload Annex 1 correctly. Using an outdated template risks administrative rejection before scientific review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission rules differ by evaluation step: applicants who receive a C or B grade at Step 1 cannot apply the following year; Step 2 non-funded applicants may reapply immediately. There is no evidence that waiting later in the eligibility window increases success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply as soon as you are eligible (as early as two years post-PhD). Feedback from unsuccessful attempts is valuable—reach to Step 2 but not funded doubles resubmission success. About 90% of unsuccessful applicants reapply within four years; many later win Consolidator Grants after Starting Grant failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence demonstration (what panels look for)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific independence is closely scrutinized: the minimum explicit evidence is one paper without your PhD advisor, but successful applicants usually present more substantial indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong evidence of independence includes last/corresponding author papers without former advisors, independent fellowships, PI funding, invited conference talks, editorial roles, single-authored reviews. Independence is evaluated relative to career stage and does not require an existing lab or permanent position.

rubrics_metrics.name: What independence does not require
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERC does not require applicants to already have their own lab, permanent position, or to be more accomplished than established senior researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame achievements relative to your career stage; preliminary data helps but is not mandatory. Emphasize trajectory and context in the CV/track record section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution and employment status
rubrics_metrics.description: You do not need to be employed by the proposed host institution when submitting; the host merely needs to commit to engaging you if the grant is awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institution prestige is not a selection criterion; scientific excellence is the sole selection criterion. Avoid assuming institutional prestige will improve selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Template structure and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Horizon Europe proposal template consists of Part A (administrative forms) and Part B (scientific proposal, max 15 pages including references). Part B1 is an extended synopsis (5 pages max). Part B2 is CV and track record (5 pages max). Early Career Achievement is 1 page max.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct year's template; annual updates introduce subtle changes. Adhere strictly to page limits and template fields to avoid administrative rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling cases with no formal viva/defense
rubrics_metrics.description: If no formal defense occurred (some doctoral systems), applicants must provide written confirmation from the awarding institution stating that no defense was organized and indicating when the PhD was officially approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This written confirmation is required to establish the reference date for eligibility calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and scan quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: All uploaded documents (support letters, employer certificates, medical documents) must be clearly legible and properly scanned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blurry scans have caused otherwise strong applications to be rejected. Ensure PDFs are readable, correctly named, and all filenames/titles (project title/acronym) match exactly across documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic timing advice based on ERC data
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical data show no advantage to waiting later in your eligibility window; applicants 4 years post-PhD have similar success rates to those 6–7 years post-PhD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply as soon as eligible to take advantage of feedback for subsequent attempts. The modal application timing has been 6 years post-PhD, but the data contradict the benefit of waiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2027 eligibility window expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned change: Starting Grant window expands from 2–7 years to 0–10 years post-PhD defense starting in 2027 (Consolidator Grant windows also shift).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates substantial overlap between grant types and new strategic choices; factor the expanded windows into long-term funding planning. Check official Work Programme for final implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official sources and where to verify rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitive rules are in the ERC Work Programme and the 'Information for Applicants to Starting and Consolidator Grant Calls' document available on the Funding & Tenders Portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex 4.4 specifically addresses PhD reference dates and extension requests. Use National Contact Points for free tailored support (eligibility verification, documentation guidance, proposal review).
